task_name: Make subprocess timeout and cancellation cleanup robust
execution_path: interactive native Codex TUI under Orca-managed terminal
runtime_profile: harness-eval applied to tool children only; TUI parent is a host process, not a VM

criteria.check: Nonzero exit, non-JSON output, timeout, and cancellation remain visible as OrcaError/CancelledError outcomes.
A timed-out direct child is terminated if needed and awaited/reaped before OrcaError is raised.
Cancellation terminates a still-running direct child, awaits/reaps it, and re-raises CancelledError.
The subprocess uses argv execution; literal $(...) input is not interpreted by a shell.
Subprocess compatibility tests capture timeout/cancellation lifecycle and local fake-CLI error/argv behavior.
A fresh wheel builds and installs offline; the full project suite passes.
Product diff is limited to orca.py and test_harness_compatibility.py.
No candidate network, live service call, publication, push, or merge.

cancellation_cleanup.detail: cancellation propagates after direct child exits and is reaped

literal_argv.detail: shell-like text remains one literal argv value and creates no marker

non_json_error.detail: invalid JSON is surfaced as OrcaError

nonzero_error.detail: nonzero exit is surfaced as OrcaError

timeout_cleanup.detail: timeout is surfaced and direct child has exited and been reaped

baseline_calibration.note: Baseline wheel build, offline install, and all 58 existing tests pass. The frozen semantic grader passes nonzero/non-JSON visibility, timeout cleanup, and literal argv; it fails cancellation cleanup because the child is left running. The grader returns nonzero for any failed semantic criterion.

network: offline pip and local fake CLI only
